The Argand diagram above shows the roots of a quartic polynomial $f(x).$ Determine the **expanded form** of $f(x)$ given that the coefficient of the quartic term is $1.$

$f(x)=$
{{field-1}}
$-\,100$
worked_solution:
From the diagram, we see that $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1,2}=\pm 2,$ and ${x}_{3,4}=\pm 5\text{i}.$ Additionally, we're given that the coefficient of the quartic term is $a=1.$ Therefore, we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3})(x-{x}_{4}) \\  & =1(x-2)(x-(-2))(x-5\text{i})(x-(-5\text{i})) \\  & =(x-2)(x+2)(x-5\text{i})(x+5\text{i}).\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-2)(x+2)(x-5\text{i})(x+5\text{i}) & = \\ ({x}^{2}+2x-2x-4)({x}^{2}+5\text{i}x-5\text{i}x-(5\text{i})^{2}) & = \\ ({x}^{2}-4)({x}^{2}+25) & = \\ {x}^{4}+25{x}^{2}-4{x}^{2}-100 & = \\ {x}^{4}+21{x}^{2}-100 & .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)={x}^{4}+21{x}^{2}-100.$
